_comment: F1-S9 slice 2 (issue #12): the mutation-testing baseline for snowflake/assert_dev_ci_grants.py + snowflake/check_forbidden_grants.py + snowflake/validate_migrations.py (the last added in the ready round -- a Codex finding: check_forbidden_grants.py directly calls validate_migrations.find_candidate_migration_files to decide which files get scanned for a forbidden PUBLIC grant, so it's genuinely part of the grant-boundary security surface, not unrelated filename/render validation). Re-measured after two later Codex findings on this same PR: (1) every python invocation in the mutation-testing and snowflake-migrations CI jobs now runs under `-P` (PYTHONSAFEPATH) to close a module-shadowing class -- see ci.yml's own comments; (2) check_forbidden_grants.py's own `from validate_migrations import ...` had to become a path-anchored importlib load (`_load_sibling_module`) since -P removes the automatic sys.path entry that bare import relied on, adding ~16 mutants to check_forbidden_grants.py's own surface (its `main()`'s pre-existing survivors are unchanged; the two NEW survivors are both inside a `# pragma: no cover`-marked, provably-unreachable defensive branch in _load_sibling_module -- equivalent mutants, not a real gap; see the function's own docstring). Earlier in this same PR's history, the bounded survivor-triage skim killed 2 real survivors (both continue -> break mutants in find_unexpected_user_role_grants, on the empty-role-field and PUBLIC-role branches respectively -- a genuine row-ordering-dependent gap where an empty-role or PUBLIC row sorting before a violating row would have silently stopped the scan; see test_assert_dev_ci_grants.py's own new tests). Re-measured on main via `mutmut run` + `mutmut export-cicd-stats` (19 Jul 2026, mutmut==3.6.0) -- deterministic across repeated runs at this final state (a rare, pre-existing 1-mutant flake was observed once during an earlier wider-scope re-measurement, always in the score-IMPROVING direction, noted in the PR body -- not present across the runs that produced this final number). check_mutation_score.py fails the check if a later run's killed/(killed+survived) ratio drops below this baseline's ratio, if total drops below this baseline's total, or if any UNRESOLVED_MUTANT_CATEGORIES count (no_tests/suspicious/timeout/segfault) rises above this baseline's (all zero here). Recorded as raw counts (not a pre-computed percentage) so a reviewer can recompute the ratio by hand and so a future re-baseline (after genuinely strengthening the test suite, or a legitimate scope change like this one) is an honest, auditable count update, not an opaque number. Per the operator scoping decision on issue #12: this starts at whatever the surface's REAL baseline is, not an aspirational target -- 593 mutants, 437 killed, 156 survived (~73.69% mutation score) as measured AT THAT TIME (F1-S9; SUPERSEDED -- the counts recorded in the fields below are the current ones, see the F1-S6 slice 9a re-measurement at the end of this comment). The four UNRESOLVED_MUTANT_CATEGORIES keys below are now RECORDED EXPLICITLY (all 0), not left to load_baseline's implicit default (independent factory-security-reviewer finding, F1-S9 slice 2, issue #12): load_baseline now fail-closes on any REQUIRED_STATS_KEYS field missing from this file, the same schema load_stats already enforces on the current run's JSON -- a rebaseline that silently OMITTED a field (e.g. 'total') would otherwise default to 0 and disable that field's regression check entirely. RE-MEASURED for F1-S6 slice 9a (issue #58, L3): `assert_sql_identifier_safe` -- the closed unquoted-identifier guard on the only two values this script interpolates into SHOW statements -- adds 21 mutants to assert_dev_ci_grants.py's surface. All 21 are killed, by TestAssertSqlIdentifierSafe plus the two TestMain tests that pin the guard ahead of connect(). Note the arithmetic against the previous baseline is killed +22 / survived -1, NOT killed +21 / survived +0: the two new TestMain tests exercise main() and incidentally kill one PRE-EXISTING survivor there as well. Getting to all-21 took two corrections, both of the same class and both worth recording because the first attempt looked adequate. Every mutant that initially survived was a STRING mutant on an operator-facing message or label, and mutmut's `XX`-wrapping form ("SNOWFLAKE_DEV_ROLE" -> "XXSNOWFLAKE_DEV_ROLEXX") cannot be killed by a substring assertion, because the corrupted value still CONTAINS the expected one. Correction 1 killed six survivors inside the guard by asserting the whole diagnostic instead of a substring. Correction 2 killed the last two -- `x_main__mutmut_38`/`_44`, the `var_name` literals at main()'s two call sites, which are the only place the label->variable binding is pinned -- by anchoring those assertions with `startswith` rather than `in`; the same fix was swept to TestAssertSqlIdentifierSafe's shared `_assert_refused` helper, which had the identical weakness. Correction 2 was found by a local `codex review` and independently by the schema-migration reviewer, AFTER correction 1 had already been committed with a (then wrong) claim that all 21 were killed -- the counts in that commit were honest measurements, the prose was not. Score RISES 0.7369 -> 0.7476. The previous baseline would have passed throughout, including while those two mutants were alive, which is exactly why it is ratcheted up here rather than left stale: a stale 593 total would also let a later change silently stop generating ~20 mutants and still clear the total-drop check. MEASURE THIS ON CI, NOT LOCALLY -- the two do not agree, and CI is authoritative because CI is the gate. A local macOS venv reports 459/155; the GitHub runner reports 458/156, and the runner's survivor set is a strict SUPERSET of the local one. The single differing mutant is `validate_migrations.x__schemachange_executable__mutmut_3`, which rewrites `shutil.which("schemachange")` to a name that cannot resolve. That is NOT a random flake, it is environment-dependent and deterministic within each environment: `_schemachange_executable` falls back to `Path(sys.executable).parent / "schemachange"`, and on the runner pip installs the console script exactly there, so the mutant returns the identical path and is behaviourally invisible (survives); in a local venv the fallback misses, behaviour diverges, and the same mutant dies. No test change can kill it on CI without making the fallback itself observable. This number is therefore pinned at the RUNNER's value, which is the pessimistic end -- a local run scoring 459 passes against it, and pinning the local 459 instead makes the required check fail on every CI run, which is exactly what happened on PR #150's first push (observed: `mutation score dropped: 0.7459 (458 killed / 614 total) is below the baseline 0.7476`). Any future rebaseline must take its numbers from a CI run's `mutation-testing-stats` artifact, never from a local run, however many times the local run repeats. Five identical local runs are not reproducibility when the disagreement is environmental. (Separately, the pre-open factory-security review measured a genuine run-to-run flip in `check_forbidden_grants.x_main__mutmut_36` in an isolated venv; that mutant survives in BOTH environments here and is not the local/CI differentiator, but a rebaseline should still confirm its state rather than assume it.)
